Welcome to Henwick Primary School
At Henwick, our values run through everything we do, and it shows — Ofsted judged our children’s behaviour as outstanding in April 2024.
We combine strong academic outcomes with rich experiences, from Year 1 Phonics and Key Stage 2 results that are significantly above national and Greenwich outcomes, to Forest School adventures and reading in our magical Rainforest Library.
Henwick is a place where every child feels at home, grows in confidence, and is inspired to learn.

Come and visit us!
Is your child starting Reception in September 2027?
Every Wednesday, from 30th September 2026 until 13th January 2027 we will be holding tours of our school for parents and carers whose children will be starting Reception in September 2027. Join us for a tour of Henwick by filling in the form below. Each tour will be led by a member of the senior leadership team.

pageCache.text:
Vision, Ethos and Values
Vision
Our vision is to remove barriers to learning, build partnerships, raise achievement and become a valued and integral part of our local and wider community.
Ethos
We are an inclusive school and we actively celebrate our rich and diverse community. We recognise the importance of developing a child’s character, nurturing their talents and inspiring their creativity. We always encourage children to be proud of who they are and recognise what they can achieve when they believe in themselves.
Values
Our values of belonging, respect, compassion, collaboration and ambition underpin everything we do and have been identified and developed by the whole school community.
The following definitions of our values were written with our children to ensure they hold meaning for everyone and that we live them every day:

Welcome to Henwick Primary School
At Henwick we are committed to the development of the whole child. The highest aspirations of all members of the school community ensure that Henwick pupils receive the very best in every aspect of their experiences here.
We are extremely proud of Henwick children and the wide variety of exciting, stimulating and challenging opportunities provided across the curriculum.
We strive to ensure that all members of our school community feel happy, safe and valued while being enable to achieve their full potential, socially and academically.
The safeguarding and welfare of our children is at the core of our beliefs and all children are aware of their rights and responsibilities.
Our aim is to ensure that the talents and strengths of every child are nurtured, encouraged, developed and celebrated and our values of belonging, respect, compassion, collaboration and ambition underpin everything we do.
I am proud to be the Executive Headteacher at Henwick Primary School and of the hard-working and confident pupils, dedicated staff and strong working relationship with parents and carers that the school benefits from.
I hope that the website will provide an insight into the caring, inclusive community that is Henwick Primary School – we welcome visitors to the school to see for yourself our learning environment.
On behalf of all staff, we look forward to welcoming and working with you and your child.
Mrs L Lazell, Executive Headteacher
Henwick Primary School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and visitors to share this commitment.

Prospective Parents
We warmly welcome you to Henwick Primary School. We are a two form entry primary school in the heart of Eltham. Our staff, governors, children and parents have the highest aspirations and expectations and are proud of their school. To get a flavour of life at Henwick and to find out some key information, please read on.
Visiting our School
We encourage prospective parents to visit the school. Formal open mornings take place in the Autumn term where prospective parents tour the school. We are happy to arrange for prospective parents to look round the school at other times and this can be arranged with the school office staff.
Outdoor Learning and Forest School
Reception outside area 25th Nov 2021 11 images
Forest School 25th Nov 2021 26 images
At Henwick we have a particular passion for learning outdoors and Forest School, we recognise its importance in the development of our children, the benefits to their learning and most importantly the fun it can bring!
When children are offered the opportunity to work and learn outside there is evidence that their confidence is boosted along with their social skills, communication, motivation, knowledge and understanding and turn taking. Children are able to learn alongside different rules and experiences than they would have in the classroom, taking risks in a safe space with trusted adults.
Children are able to get up close to nature and the adults that work alongside them are skilled in following the children’s experiences and interests in both the outside areas and the Forest School. Whilst facilitated by the adults leading the sessions, the children are able to use their imaginations’ to the max! Within our Forest School itself we have had dens built to shelter from dragons, bridges made for Superheroes and heroines, Stick people made from twigs and branches and houses made for the many bugs that are found. The mud kitchens in all of our outside areas are very popular and we have a number of budding chefs who like to explore the facilities and wide range of ingredients on offer!
Our accredited Forest School leader is incredibly experienced with a range of skills she has developed over the years. We are incredibly fortunate to have such wonderful outside learning areas as well as an extensive Forest School and it is for this reason that we access them all year round and as much as possible throughout the day. Our outside learning areas are zoned to allow for specific learning to take place in each of the spaces and this is linked to the learning which has taken place within the classroom.
Equal Opportunities
Henwick is an inclusive school and we place great importance on the need to ensure that all our pupils are included equally in opportunities for learning. The school’s ethos and the values we practice and promote aim to secure equal opportunities for all the pupils at Henwick whatever their age, gender, ethnicity, attainment and background. As a learning community all the staff work hard and are fully committed to securing the best provision for our pupils and the different groups that they may represent:
Our Policy documents and Schemes of Work are subject to regular review and the school is involved in ongoing self-evaluation to ensure that our aims and those principles that support inclusion are being appropriately implemented.

SEN Resources
At Henwick we are committed to supporting all children to access the curriculum so that they are able to achieve, make progress and enjoy experiences in line with their peers.
We are fully inclusive and strive to provide learning environments which allow children to access their learning.
Our Inclusion room is a treasure trove of resources which children are able to access throughout the day.
Some of the resources you will see around school include:
Ear Defenders
Children are able to access ear defenders as and when they need them to support with noise sensitivities and or focus.
Fidget Toys
Children are provided with fidget toys when they need support with focus or to manage sensory, emotional and cognitive experiences. Children who have an ADHD diagnosis will be offered fidget toys.
Chair Bands
Children who struggle to focus find chair bands helpful as they are able to fidget and push their feet or legs against the band which provides them with resistance and an outlet for physical activity. Children with a diagnosis or who are on the ADHD pathway will be offered a chair band.
Chew Buddies
Chew buddies provide a sensory input for the mouth and jaw, they can support with anxiety, stress, ADHD and ASD.
Wedges or Wobble Cushions
Wobble cushions support those with ASD or ADHD traits. They provide sensory input, improve focus and support with motor skill development.
Pencil Grips
Where children find they struggle with fine motor skills which impacts on their handwriting and presentation we support them with the use of pencil grips or ergonomically designed pens and pencils.
Timers
It can be difficult for some children to focus for periods of time and the different timers used for them in school allow them to see how much time is left for a task or until a transition.
Sound Buttons
Where children might struggle with cognitive overload sound buttons allow them record their sentence and listen back to it more than once allowing them to focus on the spelling, punctuation and presentation when writing it down.
Coloured Overlays
We support children who have a diagnosis of dyslexia, are on the pathway to one or who are supported by STEPS, by providing them with a coloured overlay to use when reading. These minimise the glare of black on white which reduces visual stress and improves reading comfort and fluency.
Now and Next Boards
These provide visual representations of what is happening now and what is going to happen next to support children who benefit from having clear structure and a predictable routine.
Visual Timetables
All classrooms have a visual timetable in class which has visual representations of what is happening throughout the day in order to support children who might become anxious or who benefit from a clear structure and predictable routine.
Widgets
For some children they can struggle to access the written word and process what is being communicated to them. Simple visual representations help children to process and understand communication. At Henwick we aim to ensure that all new language, signs and vocabulary is accompanied by Widgets to support with understanding.
Work Stations
At school children might benefit from a work station. These enable children to focus on their own learning, in a structured, distraction-free way.
Slope
Where children struggle with fine motor skills and in particular their handwriting and presentation, a slope might be recommended by Occupational Therapy to support.
Weighted Resources
These can provide children with sensory seeking needs the deep pressure or weight that they need to be able to focus.
Interventions
There are occasions whereby children will require time in a small group or individually with an adult to focus on specific areas or gaps in learning, communication or emotions. In school we run a number of interventions to support our children. Below are just a few examples of some of the interventions which are run alongside daily reading for fluency, maths fluency and spelling fluency interventions.
Nurture Provision
School have a Nurture Provision which supports children with understanding relationships and emotions.
Drawing and Talking
A gentle, therapeutic therapy to support children with social emotional difficulties.
Times Tables Rock Stars
An intervention to improve the fluency of times tables.
Start Write Stay Right
An Occupational Therapy based intervention to support with fine motor skills.
Zones of Regulation
An intervention to support children to understand self-regulation strategies and manage their emotions.
Lego Therapy
This intervention supports children with their use of language, communication and listening skills.
Language for Thinking
An intervention to support children develop their language and their thinking skills, enabling them to process concepts and think about events as well as developing critical thinking skills.
Wellcomm
We use this intervention to identify children who may have language difficulties and support them through the use of personalised and targeted learning tasks.

Curriculum enrichment
‘It is the essential knowledge that pupils need to be educated citizens, introducing them to the best that has been thought and said and helping to engender an appreciation of human creativity and achievement.'
– National Curriculum
By developing cultural capital, we ensure our pupils have exposure to experiences and background knowledge that will equip them with the foundations and cultural knowledge to be successful in future education and careers.
Cultural capital is developed through pupils attending events and venues as well as through their active participation. We recognise that it is vital that the children not only observe but that they actively take part to visualise themselves doing the same in the future. They can then draw on their experiences to create their own artistic impressions and creative performances as well as develop their own skills and talents based upon what they have experienced.
We are committed to providing a wide variety of exciting, stimulating and challenging opportunities across the curriculum and learning is enhanced and further embedded by the range of enrichment activities provided. School trips, visiting specialists, themed days and weeks are directly linked to topics across a range of subject areas and give pupils opportunities to learn in different environments and improve writing outcomes by enriching their vocabulary.

Reception Autumn 1

School Dinners
There are two choices of lunchtime arrangement for children at Henwick:
School dinners
The Mayor of London is ensuring all primary school children who attend state schools in London will receive free school meals for the full academic year, starting this September 2023. This means that your child and all children in our school will be entitled to free nutritious school meals next year. Please see the Dinner Arrangements Policy for further information.
Packed lunch
Eat a packed lunch brought from home. We do ask that fizzy drinks, glass bottles and sweets are not included in packed lunches
In the interests of safety, pupils who have packed lunches are reminded of the risk to other pupils of bringing in to school items of food that may trigger an allergic reaction eg peanut allergy.
At Henwick School we promote healthy eating and to support the school’s commitment to healthy lifestyles we encourage all pupils to bring water into school to drink. Water containers can be accessed throughout the school day at designated times planned by the Class teacher. All plastic drinks containers should be marked with the child’s name.
Fresh fruit is also made available each day free of charge for pupils in the Early Years and in Year 1 and Year 2.

The PTA
What is the PTA?
The Parent Teacher Association of Henwick Primary School (Henwick PTA) was formed in January 2016 and is an organisation of parents/carers and school staff. We aim to support Henwick Primary School through fundraising and social events and provide closer links between the school and parents/carers.
The structure of Henwick PTA
All parents/carers and school employees are automatically members of Henwick PTA. The PTA's current elected committee consists of:
We plan to raise money generally through events – for example a school uniform sale, Christmas fair, cake sale...We are always looking for new fundraising ideas. We would also like to organise social events for the parents/carers to get to know each other and thereby fostering the community spirit.
Vacant (Chair)
Bobbi Nolan (Treasurer)
Virginie Bit (Secretary)
Danielle Lane (Ordinary Member)
Patience Mwebaze (Ordinary Member)
How we plan to spend the money
We will always try and respond to the children’s requests; it will be great to see them having fun at the events or enjoying using a piece of new equipment that Henwick PTA will have donated. One recent wish the children expressed was to have a climbing frame in the playground; this could be our fundraising goal for the foreseeable future.
How you can help?
You are welcome to share your ideas at monthly PTA meetings which are held variably during the daytime and in the evenings to ensure that everyone can attend. You can also simply grab any of us in the playground or email HenwickPTA@outlook.com. Even half an hour of your time is a tremendous help to our community. Everyone can do their bit - helping on a stall, donating old toys or cakes for sale, helping to decorate the hall for the fair – there is plenty to do and every offer of help will be taken up.
Thank you for your support!
Did you know that you can raise money for Henwick PTA without any additional expense to yourself or your family?
EasyFundraising will donate a percentage of your online purchases directly to Henwick PTA. Raise money for the PTA while doing your weekly shop at Morrisons/Iceland/Sainsbury’s and many more. Download the Easyfundraising app and sign up to support Henwick Primary School PTA.
Another easy way of raising money is to buy a lottery ticket through yourschoollottery.co.uk . You will have a weekly chance to with the draw for our school, and also be in with a chance to win the jackpot if you match all the numbers. We have raised thousands for the school already, why not join in?

Remote Learning
The information on this page is intended to ensure parents, carers and children know what to expect from remote education where national or local restrictions require entire cohorts (or ‘bubbles’) to remain at home.
For details of what to expect where individual pupils are self-isolating, please see the final section of this page.
The remote curriculum: what is taught to pupils at home
What should my child expect from immediate remote education in the first day or two of pupils being sent home?Ready-made teaching videos from providers like Oak National Academy and White Rose will be available immediately on each child’s class blog on PurpleMash. Tasks related to the teaching videos will also be set on PurpleMash. Likewise guided reading tasks will be available from the first day. Our teachers will also record some of their own teaching videos as part of our remote learning provision but these may not be immediately ready and available on the first day or two of remote learning. We also offer paper packs to those families that request them but these will typically not be available immediately. Maths fluency practice tasks will also be available immediately on MyMaths.
Following the first few days of remote education, will my child be taught broadly the same curriculum as they would if they were in school?We teach the same curriculum remotely as we do in school wherever possible and appropriate. However, we have needed to make some adaptations in some subjects. For example, some lessons within some subjects cannot be taught easily remotely due to the specific resources or equipment needed such as some science lessons, PE lessons or maths lessons.
Remote teaching and study time each day
How long can I expect work set by the school to take my child each day?We expect that remote education (including remote teaching and independent work) will take pupils broadly the following number of hours each day:
Three hours a day on average
Four hours a day on average
Accessing remote education
How will my child access any online remote education you are providing?We use PurpleMash to share links to teaching videos and set related tasks that children can submit for feedback. Guided reading tasks and quizzes are also set on this platform. We also use MyMaths for children to access maths fluency tasks and the daily live sessions are delivered with Microsoft Teams. Some additional sessions for children with additional needs, such as STEPS interventions, are delivered via Teams as well.
If my child does not have digital or online access at home, how will you support them to access remote education?We recognise that some pupils may not have suitable online access at home. We take the following approaches to support those pupils to access remote education:
How will my child be taught remotely?We use a combination of the following approaches to teach pupils remotely:
Pre-recorded video lessons made by our teachers
Printed paper packs produced by teachers
Engagement and feedback
What are your expectations for my child’s engagement and the support that we as parents and carers should provide at home?Our expectations are that children join the live sessions each day, watch the videos set by the teachers and complete and submit the related tasks.
Parents and carers can support children with helping to keep to a consistent routine, helping them with any technical issues and, if and when possible, watching some of the videos with them and discussing them with the children.
How will you check whether my child is engaging with their work and how will I be informed if there are concerns?Each day, teaching assistants take a register of who has joined the live session and also who has submitted tasks that day. This is entered into an online form and the senior leadership and pastoral teams monitor this to see who is engaging regularly and who isn’t and any patterns that are forming.
Likewise, teachers also inform the senior leadership and pastoral teams about children who they are concerned about.
The senior leadership and pastoral teams also ask teachers for updates about engagement to get more detail about the type of work a child is engaging with, e.g. if they are just completing quizzes but not the more in-depth tasks set.
Any concerns relating to engaging with work or otherwise are followed up with a phone call either from the senior leadership and pastoral teams or the class teacher.
How will you assess my child’s work and progress?Feedback can take many forms and may not always mean extensive written comments for individual children. For example, whole-class feedback or quizzes marked automatically via digital platforms are also valid and effective methods, amongst many others. Our approach to feeding back on pupil work is as follows:
Fluency practice on MyMaths is automatically marked.
Additional support for pupils with particular needs
How will you work with me to help my child who needs additional support from adults at home to access remote education?
We recognise that some pupils, for example some pupils with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), may not be able to access remote education without support from adults at home. We acknowledge the difficulties this may place on families, and we will work with parents and carers to support those pupils in the following ways:
Remote education for self-isolating pupils
Where individual pupils need to self-isolate but the majority of their peer group remains in school, how remote education is provided will likely differ from the approach for whole groups. This is due to the challenges of teaching pupils both at home and in school.
If my child is not in school because they are self-isolating, how will their remote education differ from the approaches described above?
When a single child is isolating but the teacher and the rest of the class remain in school full time, a personal blog will be set up on PurpleMash and work will be set using readymade teaching videos, such as Oak National Academy and White Rose Maths. Teachers will not be making their own pre-recorded teaching videos in this situation.

What is TFL Stars?
STARS is TFL's accreditation scheme for London schools and nurseries. STARS inspires young Londoners to travel to school sustainably, actively, responsibly and safely by championing walking, scooting and cycling. STARS supports pupils' wellbeing, helps to reduce congestion at the school gates and improve road safety and air quality.
What is TFL Stars accreditation?
If Junior Travel Ambassador’s are successful in completing a range of activities to promote healthier travel in their community, they can apply to receive the TFL Stars gold, silver or bronze award.
Who are the Junior Travel Ambassador’s?
Our Junior Travel Ambassador team are a proactive group of children from Year 5 and Year 6 who have given their free time to work alongside Travel Champions to promote, build awareness and participate in travel issues in and around out school.
Joining over half the school’s in London, Henwick’s Junior Travel Ambassadors have worked towards making their environment healthier and safer by recognising ways to improving road safety and the health and wellbeing of members of our school community.
What activities have the Junior Travel Ambassador's been involved with?
Our Ambassadors work busily on many activities throughout the year including giving feedback, conducting surveys, planning activities and creating positive attitudes to travel under the guidance and support of our local borough representatives.
